strategy: Two-tier. (1) A small, hand-verified list of permanent redirects — wired into next.config.ts `redirects()` — for the handful of legacy URLs whose destination on the new site is unambiguous. (2) Everything else that matches a legacy WordPress post slug falls through to the `[legacySlug]` catch-all route (src/app/[legacySlug]/page.tsx), which looks the slug up in migration/full-legacy-manifest.json and renders a metadata-only 'legacy archive record' notice — title, date, category, classification-appropriate note — rather than either a bare 404 or a blanket redirect to the homepage. Records classified SPAM render a real 404 (not indexed, not shown) rather than any page at all.

behavior.SPAM: notFound() — served as a real 404, not indexed. ~2,488 records.
behavior.everythingElse: Metadata-only 'legacy archive record' page: title, original publish date, category, migration classification, and — for SYNDICATED records — source publisher attribution. No article body is reproduced. Page is marked noindex except for the 3 OWNED historical records, which redirect via the wired list above instead of hitting this route.

explicitlyNotDone: This does not redirect all ~11,837 legacy URLs individually, and does not redirect unmatched URLs to the homepage. Per the migration brief, blanket-redirecting an entire spam-and-syndication-heavy archive to the homepage would be poor SEO practice and would misrepresent unreviewed content as current reporting.
